Technical Note

Photonic Computing and Fault Simulation

Independent Research and Development · Interactive Demonstration · Interactive prototype

Inject phase and attenuation faults into a four-channel, four-stage MZI mesh and quantify changes in output power.

Discuss a similar project Run the four-stage MZI mesh Technical diagram

Industry problem and engineering challenge

Photonic systems are sensitive to phase errors and insertion loss. Early design work needs a way to examine how changes in components affect the output. A software model should specify how it defines loss, amplitude and power so that future device measurements can be compared with its predictions.

Technical approach and architecture

Implementation and deliverables

A complex transfer-matrix model calculates both ideal and faulty fields in a four-stage MZI mesh. Visitors can choose the input, fault stage and component, phase and power attenuation.

Outcome

Follow propagation through each stage and compare per-port power, total output and relative output error with the same input.

  • Interactive simulation of one interferometer
  • Component assumptions and validation checks

Validation and evidence

Analytic cases, zero input, lossless energy conservation, boundary parameters and independent complex reference vectors validate the implementation.

Numerical simulation of a four-channel, four-stage ideal MZI mesh.

Public evidence classification · Interactive prototype

Software simulation

Four-channel, four-stage fault propagation

Select a component and vary phase and power attenuation. Compare the ideal and faulty outputs at each stage. Analytic cases and independent complex-matrix reference values validate the model.
